title: Families Reunite After Evacuation From Oleshky
summary:
Residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have crossed into Ukrainian-held territory after a humanitarian mission and a localized ceasefire, Ukrainian officials said.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the Ukrainian citizens from Oleshky had crossed in the Chernihiv region and that all of them will receive the assistance they need. He thanked the U.S. and Melania Trump for mediation.

The residents travelled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus. Russia's Ministry of Defence said those travelling to Ukrainian-held territory were taken to the Russian city of Anapa and flown to the Belarusian city of Homel, accompanied by Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's commissioner for human rights.

Ukrainian authorities did not permit disclosure of the number of evacuees or the exact location of the border crossing. Ukrainian organizers said the restrictions were imposed in part to safeguard residents who chose to remain in Oleshky and to protect similar humanitarian missions that may occur.

The ceasefire in Ukraine's southern Kherson region began at 3 a.m. local time on Tuesday and is expected to continue through Sunday evening. Civilians from Oleshky, on the Dnipro River, began the journey in bus convoys on Friday. The estimated 2,000 remaining residents were offered the choice of travelling to Ukrainian- or Russian-held territory, or remaining in the city with replenished food and medical supplies, the article says.

On Saturday, relatives waited at the border between Ukraine and Belarus, along with aid tents, coffee stands and provisions to feed pets evacuees were bringing. Volunteers from organizations including the Red Cross, Doctors Without Borders and World Central Kitchen were also there.

Among those waiting was Liza Paliy, 19, who last saw her father more than two years ago. She, her mother and sister had left at the time, while he stayed behind, expecting, she said, to return within a month or two.
why_it_matters: The mission reunited families who had been separated for more than two years. It also shows how temporary ceasefires and mediation can create a safe path for civilians.

background_read: Oleshky is a city in Ukraine's southern Kherson region that is occupied by Russia, and its residents have been separated from family members in Ukrainian-held territory.
A humanitarian mission is an organised effort to help civilians, and a localized ceasefire can pause fighting in one area so people can travel safely.
For this journey, residents travelled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus to reach Ukrainian-held territory.
Aid organisations and volunteers waited at the border with tents, food and provisions so families could reunite and receive help.
